question: The Fundamental Principles of the Olympic Charter are based on a document written by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pierre de Coubertin.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Principles of the Olympic Charter are based on a document written by Pierre de Coubertin.
 
• He is a French educator and historian, founder of the International Olympic Committee, and its second president.
 
• He is known as the father of the modern Olympic Games. 
 
• He was born into a French aristocratic family, he became an academic and studied a broad range of topics, most notably education and history.
 
• He graduated with a degree in law and public affairs from the Paris Institute of Political Studies (Sciences Po).
 
• It was at Sciences Po that he came up with the idea of the Summer Olympic Games.
 
• The Pierre de Coubertin medal (also known as the Coubertin medal or the True Spirit of Sportsmanship medal) is an award given by the International Olympic Committee to athletes who demonstrate the spirit of sportsmanship in the Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Olympic Games

 
 
• The first occurrence of the modern Olympic Games was the Athens Games.
 
• From 6 April to 15 April 1896, an athletic festival was held in Athens.
 
• Around 280 athletes, attended the inaugural Games of the Modern Olympics.
 
• The athletes competed in 43 events.
 
• Every year on 23rd June World Olympic Day is celebrated to promote the idea of the Olympics.
